rv.q: This terrific coming-of-age comedy can allow a retro laugh or two alongside its heartache and its warmth.
Nikolai Foster's beautifully acted revival is totally attuned to the play's swirling mix of emotion and hilarity.

Suranne Jones and Oliver Farnworth as the adult lovers have great comic timing but less nuance: a pity, in Jones's case, for there is a sense of unexplored depths in her relationship with her son, which trembles between overpowering love and an almost sexualised hostility. As a drama, Beautiful Thing hasn't much of a narrative arc.
The moments of awkward discovery and eventual acceptance are beautifully done but are sadly too brief.
Beautiful Thing is in danger of losing its immediacy for a new generation of spectators and turning into a largely nostalgic pleasure for an older one.

cn.t: Harvey's tender gay love story retains its wit and emotional punch two decades on, though some critics find the production uneven and wish for deeper exploration of its themes beyond period nostalgia.
